# pbs_s3_endpoint (Resource)

Manages a Proxmox Backup Server S3 endpoint: the connection to an S3-compatible object store — Amazon S3, Ceph RGW, MinIO, Backblaze B2, Cloudflare R2 and the like — that datastores on S3 keep their backups in. A `pbs_datastore` names it in `backend.client`.

PBS contacts nothing when it saves an endpoint: wrong keys or a wrong fingerprint show when a datastore uses the endpoint, or when the `pbs_s3_buckets` data source lists its buckets; a wrong region shows when a datastore uses it, and in the list only where the object store checks the region requests are signed for.

S3 endpoints exist from PBS 4.0. Datastores on S3 were a technology preview until PBS 4.1.9.

~> **PBS refuses to delete an endpoint a datastore uses.** Destroy the datastore first. A datastore's `backend` cannot change, so a change of `id`, which replaces the endpoint, replaces its datastores too.

Managing endpoints needs `Sys.Modify` on `/system/s3-endpoint`, or on `/system/s3-endpoint/<id>` for an existing one; reading them `Sys.Audit`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Amazon S3 in eu-central-1, for datastores on S3. PBS puts a datastore's
# bucket into the host name, in place of {{bucket}}, and the region in place
# of {{region}}, so one endpoint serves every bucket the access key reaches.
# The buckets and the access key are created at AWS: PBS creates neither, and
# contacts nothing when it saves the endpoint.
resource "pbs_s3_endpoint" "aws" {
  id         = "aws"
  endpoint   = "{{bucket}}.s3.{{region}}.amazonaws.com"
  region     = "eu-central-1"
  access_key = "AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE"

  # The secret key is write-only: it never reaches the plan or state, and
  # PBS receives it when the endpoint is created and whenever
  # secret_key_wo_version changes.
  secret_key_wo         = var.aws_secret_access_key
  secret_key_wo_version = 1

  # All datastores on the endpoint together upload at most 50 MB per second,
  # leaving bandwidth for the rest (PBS 4.1+). Traffic control rules do not
  # limit what PBS sends to S3.
  rate_out = "50MB"
}

# MinIO in the local network, with a self-signed certificate on port 9000.
# Like Ceph RGW, it takes the bucket in the path of a request rather than in
# the host name.
resource "pbs_s3_endpoint" "minio" {
  id         = "minio"
  endpoint   = "minio.example.com"
  port       = 9000
  path_style = true
  access_key = "pbs"

  # The certificate's SHA-256 fingerprint, as
  # `openssl x509 -noout -fingerprint -sha256 -in public.crt` shows it. Leave
  # it out for a certificate of a public CA.
  fingerprint = "7c:47:fd:cb:f4:62:f9:0e:93:ad:74:5f:39:fe:c4:d2:f7:4f:d9:6e:1d:af:f8:ae:ae:9a:ad:ff:95:19:62:50"

  secret_key_wo         = var.minio_secret_key
  secret_key_wo_version = 1
}

variable "aws_secret_access_key" {
  description = "Secret access key of AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE at AWS."
  type        = string
  sensitive   = true
  ephemeral   = true
}

variable "minio_secret_key" {
  description = "Secret key of the access key pbs on minio.example.com."
  type        = string
  sensitive   = true
  ephemeral   = true
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `access_key` (String, Sensitive) Access key ID PBS signs its requests with. PBS returns it, so a change made outside Terraform shows in the next plan; it is kept in state, marked sensitive.
- `endpoint` (String) Host name or IP address of the object store, without a scheme, port or path, such as `s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com`. PBS replaces `{{bucket}}`, which may only start it, with the bucket, and `{{region}}` with `region`: `{{bucket}}.s3.{{region}}.amazonaws.com`, say. PBS connects over HTTPS only.
- `id` (String) Endpoint ID, 3 to 32 characters: letters, digits, `_`, `.` and `-`, not starting with `.` or `-`. Datastores name it in `backend.client`. Changing it replaces the endpoint.

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `burst_in` (String) How many bytes over `rate_in` PBS may download at once, after a quiet period; as much as `rate_in` when left out. PBS ignores it without `rate_in`. Needs PBS 4.1 or newer. A byte size such as `500`, `64KiB`, `10MiB` or `1.5GB`: `K`, `M`, `G`, `T` and `P` are powers of 1000, `Ki` to `Pi` powers of 1024, and `B` is optional. PBS writes it back in its own spelling, such as `10 MiB`, which counts as the same: state keeps the configuration's. Only after an import, state has PBS's spelling, and the next plan shows an update that sends nothing.
- `burst_out` (String) How many bytes over `rate_out` PBS may upload at once, after a quiet period; as much as `rate_out` when left out. PBS ignores it without `rate_out`. Needs PBS 4.1 or newer. A byte size such as `500`, `64KiB`, `10MiB` or `1.5GB`: `K`, `M`, `G`, `T` and `P` are powers of 1000, `Ki` to `Pi` powers of 1024, and `B` is optional. PBS writes it back in its own spelling, such as `10 MiB`, which counts as the same: state keeps the configuration's. Only after an import, state has PBS's spelling, and the next plan shows an update that sends nothing.
- `fingerprint` (String) SHA-256 fingerprint of the object store's certificate, for a self-signed one: 64 hexadecimal digits, optionally separated by colons, in either case. PBS then accepts the certificate with this fingerprint; a certificate its system's CAs validate it accepts either way, so the fingerprint is no pin against those. When left out, PBS accepts only certificates its CAs validate. The fingerprint changes with the certificate, so update it when the certificate is renewed or replaced.
- `limit_active_requests` (Number) How many `PUT`, `POST` and `DELETE` requests a second the datastores on this endpoint send to the object store together, at most; no limit when left out. Needs PBS 4.2.4 or newer, which also deprecated the `put-rate-limit` before it: the provider leaves that alone. Before PBS 4.2.7, `limit_passive_requests` replaced this limit when both were set.
- `limit_passive_requests` (Number) How many `GET` and `HEAD` requests a second the datastores on this endpoint send to the object store together, at most; no limit when left out. Needs PBS 4.2.4 or newer.
- `path_style` (Boolean) Whether PBS addresses a bucket in the path of its requests, `https://<endpoint>/<bucket>/…`, as MinIO and Ceph RGW usually need, rather than in the host name, `https://<bucket>.<endpoint>/…`. Defaults to `false`.
- `port` (Number) Port of the object store; 443, HTTPS's, when left out.
- `provider_quirks` (Set of String) Features of the S3 API the object store lacks, which PBS then works around: `skip-if-none-match-header`, for a store that does not understand the `If-None-Match` header, and `delete-objects-via-delete-object`, for one without the `DeleteObjects` call, which PBS then replaces by one request per object; that one needs PBS 4.1.6 or newer.
- `rate_in` (String) Rate limit on the data the datastores on this endpoint download from the object store together, in bytes per second; no limit when left out. Needs PBS 4.1 or newer. A byte size such as `500`, `64KiB`, `10MiB` or `1.5GB`: `K`, `M`, `G`, `T` and `P` are powers of 1000, `Ki` to `Pi` powers of 1024, and `B` is optional. PBS writes it back in its own spelling, such as `10 MiB`, which counts as the same: state keeps the configuration's. Only after an import, state has PBS's spelling, and the next plan shows an update that sends nothing.
- `rate_out` (String) Rate limit on the data the datastores on this endpoint upload to the object store together, in bytes per second; no limit when left out. Needs PBS 4.1 or newer. A byte size such as `500`, `64KiB`, `10MiB` or `1.5GB`: `K`, `M`, `G`, `T` and `P` are powers of 1000, `Ki` to `Pi` powers of 1024, and `B` is optional. PBS writes it back in its own spelling, such as `10 MiB`, which counts as the same: state keeps the configuration's. Only after an import, state has PBS's spelling, and the next plan shows an update that sends nothing.
- `region` (String) Region of the object store, such as `eu-central-1`, which requests are signed for and which replaces `{{region}}` in `endpoint`: 2 to 32 characters, lower-case letters, digits, `_` and `-`, not starting with `-`. PBS signs for `us-west-1` when left out.
- `secret_key_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Secret key of `access_key`. PBS needs it to create the endpoint, so it is required then; after an import, leave it out to keep the secret key PBS has. Write-only: Terraform passes it to PBS without storing it in the plan or state, and PBS never returns it, so a change made outside Terraform goes unnoticed. PBS receives it when the object is created and whenever `secret_key_wo_version` changes. Requires `secret_key_wo_version`, and Terraform or OpenTofu 1.11 or later.
- `secret_key_wo_version` (Number) Version of `secret_key_wo`, which Terraform stores in its place. Change it — increment it, say — to send a new `secret_key_wo`; removing it, with `secret_key_wo`, leaves the value on the server as it is. Requires `secret_key_wo`.
- `use_node_proxy` (Boolean) Whether PBS connects to the object store through the HTTP proxy of its node configuration. Defaults to `false`, a direct connection. `true` needs PBS 4.2.4 or newer; from 4.1.7 to 4.2.3, PBS always uses the node's proxy, whatever this says.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = pbs_s3_endpoint.aws
  identity = {
    id = "aws"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `id` (String) S3 endpoint ID, such as `backblaze`.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = pbs_s3_endpoint.aws
  id = "aws"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# S3 endpoints are imported by ID. PBS never returns the secret key, so
# secret_key_wo_version is empty after an import: leave secret_key_wo and
# secret_key_wo_version out to keep the secret key PBS has, as a
# configuration that sets them sends secret_key_wo in the next apply.
terraform import pbs_s3_endpoint.aws aws
```
